proven_findings.evidence: The shortcut is attempted only when player field +0xB0 is positive and the 0x0800 bit in the word at +0x6F4 is clear.
The current input buffer and session index are passed to the bounded entity/alias matcher at 0x0046ABB4; null falls through to later command processing.
The 16-bit value at player offset +0x92 is passed to the hashed record resolver at 0x00432BD3 and the returned record must be non-null.
The selector begins as 0x6C and remains 0x6C only when the resolved record word at +0x40 equals 5.
For every resolved record type other than 5, subtracting 0x4D converts selector 0x6C to 0x1F.
The player record, selected action id, and zero mode argument are passed to 0x00461273; a zero result falls through and a nonzero result completes the gameplay input as handled.
0x00461273 explicitly branches on selector 0x1F and 0x6C, proving two related execution modes.
The 0x6C branch requires record type 5 and emits KAI/invoke-specific diagnostics including 'You may not invoke... You are not KAI!' and 'Syntax: INVOKE {power} [{target}]'.
The 0x1F branch rejects record type 5 and emits cast-specific diagnostics including 'You may not cast... You are KAI!' and 'You have no spells to cast!'.
A successful entity-name match is immediately converted into CAST or INVOKE execution, establishing an implicit target shortcut before later general command handling.
